newsitem.title: FINLAND: Kone says price competition still tough.
newsitem.headline: Kone says price competition still tough.

text.p: Finnish elevator maker Kone Oy said on Thursday it may book slightly higher orders in 1996 than in 1995 but prices would remain poor.

"Price competition continues to be extremely tough in all geographical areas and business sectors," Kone said in a statement with its January-August results, which showed a 79 percent slump in profit after financial items to 14 million markka.
The main drag on Kone's January-August profit was tougher-than-expected problems in Kone's Italian operations. @

Kone's report included from July 1 the results of German escalator maker O&K Rolltreppen acquired in summer, but the company said much of the German company's sales were already handled by various Kone companies so its impact was slight.
Kone said it expected full-year 1996 sales to reach about 10 billion markka at current exchange rates, up from 9.52 billion in 1995.

Its total sales in January-August rose by some seven percent to 6.01 billion markka. Kone said new elevator and escalator sales accounted for about 34 percent of total turnover with maintenance and modernisation making up the remainder. @

Kone said the value of new orders excluding maintenance sales rose by about 10 percent to 4.87 billion. It said this increase would only have been about four percent without new acquisitions and the impact of currency fluctuations.
"Orders received for the whole of 1996 will probably exceed slightly those for the previous year, but the price level will remain poor," Kone said.
Demand for its new space-saving elevator concept had got off to a promising start: "Its impact on Kone's result, however, will only become tangible in future years." @

Kone said prices in the maintenance sector had continued under downward pressure. "Nevertheless, the profitability of maintenance operations has been sustained through productivity improvement," it said.
